---
title: "Computation and coordination"
description: "Why the experimental process needs a representation of its own, and why that representation extends BPMN rather than replacing it."
---

Reproducibility is usually pursued as documentation: a preregistration beside the study, a methods section about the study, a checklist attached to the manuscript. Each is a separate artifact carrying its own partial copy of the design, and nothing holds the copies to each other.

The alternative is to make reproducibility a property *of* the shared artifact rather than of the documents beside it. That is what Studyflow is for, and this page gives the argument.

## The gap is in the process

Drift has been measured at every stage of a study's life. Nine of 67 audited trials reported their outcomes faithfully[^compare]. Eleven of 35 open-data articles reproduced without help from their authors[^hardwicke]. Twenty-nine teams given one question and one dataset returned odds ratios from 0.89 to 2.93[^many]. Seventy teams analyzing a single neuroimaging dataset produced no two identical workflows[^variability].

These studies followed good practice. The failure is structural rather than motivational: the process was never written in a form anything could check.

| Standardized today | Not standardized today |
|:--|:--|
| how data are formatted, organized, named, and shared | the order steps run in, and what decides the order |
| the columns of a trial table, the layout of an imaging session | which participants were eligible, and how arms were allocated |
| the vocabulary a dataset is described with | where a participant could leave, and what happened to their data |
| the archive a dataset is deposited in | which analysis was fixed in advance, and which was chosen after looking |

Data standards are necessary and not sufficient: studies that share standardized data still fail to replicate.

## A program has two halves

A complete programming model has a **computation model** and a **coordination model** — the part that binds individual activities into an ensemble[^gelernter]. Ordinary code has a first-class notation for the first and none for the second: ordering, dependencies, and what each stage hands the next end up spread through call graphs and shared state. Machine learning has documented the result as glue code and pipeline jungles, where changing anything changes everything[^sculley].

Coordination is exactly where a study's drift accumulates, because it is the half that also has to be described to an ethics board, registered, drawn for a paper, and reconstructed by a replicator — four descriptions of something the code never states in one place.

Studyflow is a coordination language for experimental studies. The computations stay in the tools built for them; the notation carries the coordination that currently lives in preregistrations, manuscripts, slides, and glue code.

| Stays where it is | Moves into the notation |
|:--|:--|
| presenting a stimulus, in jsPsych, PsychoPy, lab.js, or a game engine | which task follows which, and under what condition |
| fitting a model, in Python or R | which step reads which data, and what it writes back |
| a call to a language model | who takes part, and which arm they were assigned |
| the text of a consent form | that nothing may run before consent is given |

## Why extend BPMN

A recurring domain structure, many notations for it, and no shared one is the classic case for a domain-specific language rather than general-purpose code[^mernik]. Studyflow does not invent one. It extends BPMN 2.0, standardized as ISO/IEC 19510[^bpmn], and inherits three things a new notation would have to earn:

| Inherited | What it means here |
|:--|:--|
| A control-flow vocabulary with defined semantics | events, activities, gateways, boundary events, sub-processes, pools, and choreography already mean something precise |
| A serialization fixed by a standard body | the file outlives any one tool or vendor, this project included |
| An extension mechanism | added types and attributes ride in places the standard reserves for them, so a generic BPMN tool still reads the file and ignores the rest |

Two decisions hold the cost down for a researcher who does not know BPMN. First, an author works in domain terms — a cognitive task, a questionnaire, a randomization gateway — not in BPMN's generic vocabulary. Second, execution semantics come from the Studyflow specification rather than from a third-party process engine, so running a studyflow requires no further tooling.

## What Studyflow does not replace

| Neighbouring tool | What it owns | What Studyflow adds |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Experiment builders and task scripts | the trial, the stimulus, the runtime | the consent, eligibility, allocation, and data flow around them |
| Workflow engines | executing computation graphs at scale | a study's cycles, interrupts, and human steps, and a definition a reviewer can read |
| Data standards | the shape of what was collected | the process that produced it, referenced to those standards |
| Provenance standards | a record of what ran | a plan written in advance, in the same object as its record |
| Reporting guidelines | which items must be reported | the items attached to the steps they describe, so coverage follows the design |

A study needs both a procedural flow — conditions, phases, approvals — and a data flow, from raw through cleaned to analyzed. [The studyflow object](object.qmd) carries both over one shared set of nodes.
